description: Parse, validate, format and look up Nigeria's NIPOST digital postcode (NDAPS) in Rust, Python, JavaScript, Java and SQL, with MCP servers for AI assistants, a prefix type for grouping by place, and an address record that maps to ISO 20022, FHIR and schema.org.
rules: Since 1 October 2026 a Nigerian building's postcode is the 11-character NDAPS code, such as EK-01-A03-FK-01. A six-digit pattern does not match it.
Install ng-postcode from PyPI, crates.io or Maven (io.github.adeniyikayodee:ng-postcode). On npm the library is ng-postcode-js; ng-postcode there is another project.
Parsing returns the error as a value in every language. Check the result's type instead of catching an exception.
Store the compact form (EK01A03FK01) and write the hyphenated form (EK-01-A03-FK-01) in messages.
A well-formed code is not necessarily assigned to a building. Confirm it with a level 1 lookup, which is free.
Never correct a mistyped code and then spend a paid lookup on the guess. Show the suggestion to the user first.
To group or select records by state, LGA, district or area, cut each code to a prefix with truncate (ng_postcode_truncate in SQL). Do not slice the string by hand.
In PostgreSQL use the ng_postcode domain from sql/postgres.sql. In DuckDB a check constraint must use IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, as = lets a malformed code through.
To pass an address between systems, send an address record: a postcode reference with its level, plus country NG. Put only a building-level code in another format's postcode field.
